source.title: A view of mini-batch SGD via generating functions: conditions of convergence, phase transitions, benefit from negative momenta
source.authors: Maksim Velikanov; Denis Kuznedelev; D. Yarotsky

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices and experimental sections; no apparent cutoff affecting the study.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies noise-averaged training-loss convergence and SGD stability for linear and linearized regression models. It does not test whether networks that memorize random labels generalize on natural labels, nor the listed train–test gap conditions or measures.
record.gate_note: The reported outcomes concern training loss, its convergence or divergence, and spectral approximation of SGD dynamics. These do not measure held-out test error, a train–test gap, or any of V1–V8. Experiments comparing approximation regimes and batch sizes therefore do not qualify as rows for these versions.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes SGD training-loss convergence, stability and hyperparameter choices, not any of V1–V8. Batch-size comparisons report training loss rather than held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets. Its spectral and approximation-error measures do not measure generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors develop a spectral framework for noise-averaged mini-batch SGD training loss in linear models and linearized networks. Under the Spectrally Expressible approximation, they derive stability conditions and power-law loss behavior, and show that negative momentum can help in some noise-dominated regimes. Experiments assess these optimization predictions; they do not establish held-out generalization results.
record.recipe_differences: Analyzes mini-batch SGD with momentum on quadratic objectives for linear models and linearized networks, focusing on training-loss dynamics rather than generalization error.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-loss convergence and divergence depend on spectral distributions, learning rate, momentum, batch-size-related sampling noise, and the SE approximation parameter. The accuracy of the SE approximation varies by dataset and setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix E.5 and Figure 5 show approximately equal MNIST training loss at equal computation budget bt across batch sizes when learning rate scales with batch size, with diminishing returns at large batches.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mini-batch SGD can exhibit approximately linear batch-size scalability for training-loss optimization up to a workload-dependent scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Sections 5–6 derive spectral conditions for training-loss convergence and show that negative momentum can improve convergence in some noise-dominated regimes, supported by synthetic experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The stability and optimal momentum of mini-batch SGD depend on spectral structure and sampling noise.

record.problems: The analysis of realistic problems depends on the Spectrally Expressible approximation, which the paper says is not exact in general and whose accuracy varies by dataset. Experiments use subsets of MNIST (typically 1,000–10,000 examples) because of computational costs. The reported outcomes are training-loss results, not evidence about held-out generalization.
record.rows_left_out: No rows qualify: reported experimental outcomes measure training loss, optimization stability, or approximation accuracy, not the behavior measured by V1–V8.
